hero.title: Tirthankaras of Jainism: Ancient Ascetics
hero.description: An in-depth exploration of the 24 Tirthankaras who laid the philosophical and ascetic foundation of the Jain tradition in ancient India.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Philosophy

  • Ahimsa (Non-violence)
  • Aparigraha (Non-possession)
  • Satya (Truth)

Key Figures

  • Rishabhanatha (Adinatha)
  • Parshvanatha
  • Mahavira
  • Evolution of Jainism
    • First Tirthankara: Rishabhanatha (Founder/First Teacher)
    • Historical Validation: Parshvanatha (23rd) and Mahavira (24th)
    • Systematization: Mahavira reorganized the sangha
TirthankaraSymbolSignificance

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Understanding the transition from legendary figures to historically verifiable personalities in Jain antiquity.

cards.details: The era of Rishabhanatha, the first Tirthankara, often associated with the dawn of civilization in Indian texts.
Parshvanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara, is historically accepted by scholars as a real historical figure.
Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara, a contemporary of Gautama Buddha.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Key memory aids for remembering symbols and names.

items.title: R-A-S-N-M
items.decryption: Remember these as the 1st (Bull), 2nd (Elephant), 3rd (Horse), 22nd (Conch), and 24th (Lion) to tackle matching-type questions.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not assume all 24 Tirthankaras are historical. Only the 23rd and 24th have clear historical validation.
Confusing Tirthankara symbols is common; focus on the 1st, 22nd, 23rd, and 24th specifically.
Rishabhanatha is often erroneously attributed to Vedic origins; he is explicitly mentioned in the Rig Veda but belongs to the Shramana tradition.
